label: Balance
title: Balance
summary: Use a Balance to show one money amount, such as what someone owes or holds, in large type under a short title.
corePrinciple: One amount, named, at a glance.

sizing.title: The host sets the width, Context3 the amount
sizing.description: A Balance is as wide as its host and as tall as its text: 68 px at the default size. It has no padding or surface, so place it in a screen or card that has them. Context3 sets the amount’s size; the title stays 14 px.

content.title: Say what it is, write it as people read it
content.description: Write the title as a short name for the amount, such as “Available balance” or “Total owed to people”. Pass the amount already formatted, with separators and decimals: the Balance shows it exactly as you write it.

inContext.title: What you owe after a trip
inContext.description: The trip screen adds up what you owe and passes it as formatted text; the Balance only shows it. Settle up is the screen’s own Button.

sources.title: Use the public Balance contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (27 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Balance is one component with a Title property and a nested Money Value; the package adds amount and currency props and a slot for your own Money Value. Figma draws the amount on a 36 px line, the package on a 44 px one, so a Balance is 68 px tall instead of 60. The package’s default amount is “50,000.67”, as in Figma and Storybook. A Money Value in the slot always gets Context3 Balance & Cards. Page type JioPlus turns both the title and the amount white. On the web the amount is announced once, with its currency, such as “₹50,000.67”. The published Storybook docs page for Balance still doesn’t load: the fix is in Biscuit’s source but not yet deployed; its stories load.
